alex: heads-up — noticed a perf regression on master during canary runs. tight-window batcher spikes KV resident and trips soft-oom on several GPUs :grimacing:
jia: ugh, when did this start?
matt: saw it around the kernel-selection refactor yesterday afternoon. can repro with the short-seq traffic replay.
perf-bot: [canary-run-5678] metric snapshot: kv_resident=12.3GB -> 13.9GB, avg_batch_tokens=420 -> 510, kernel_switches/sec +37%
jia: can you paste the small profiler output?
matt: paste below — shows batch formation holding on token budget and then a kernel handoff flood.
```
[2026-03-18 14:02:11] batcher: admit window=40ms, target_tokens=512, formed_batches=278
[2026-03-18 14:02:11] kv: resident=13.9GB, slab_frag=18%, free_headroom=550MB
[2026-03-18 14:02:11] kernel: chosen=fast-matmul, latency_p50=6.2ms, p95=18.4ms
[2026-03-18 14:02:11] kernel: fallback_attempts=21 -> cpu-kernel (short seq path)
[2026-03-18 14:02:11] oom_guard: soft_oom_margin_triggered=true, throttle_count=43
```
sam: that slab_frag number is worrying. looks like KV fragmentation + tight windows = bursty headroom loss.
alex: my brain: when batches form quickly we oversubscribe KV slots before the allocator can compact/evict. need admission hysteresis not just a single headroom check.
jia: propose two changes to test in canary: 1) reduce token_budget_target for tight-window class from 512 -> 320; 2) add OOM-signal hysteresis: require two consecutive soft_oom events within 10s before full reject, otherwise do soft-shrink (reduce batch token cap by 25%).
matt: also propose kernel-handoff throttle: if kv_free_headroom < 800MB then prefer low-memory kernel variant or preemptive eviction async and avoid switching kernels mid-batch. avoids double-scratch.
sam: agree. add a small gate on kernel_switches/sec > 10 to suppress noncritical handoffs.
alex: can we roll these as a single feature-flagged canary? I can push a flag in the config service. command: `curl -X POST $CONFIG_SVC/flags -d '{"name":"tight_window_kv_mitigation","value":true}'`
perf-bot: queued canary job -> https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/7890 (will run 1h ramp w/ short-seq traffic)
matt: note for experiment: record these counters per-batch: pre_admit_headroom, post_admit_headroom, kernel_route_id, kernel_switch_count, kv_evictions_async
jia: ack. i'll add logging and a compact debug trace that only samples 1/500 requests.
sam: if canary looks good we should backfill a microbenchmark to reproduce fragmentation quickly (force many short prefixes + random kv touch) to validate compaction heuristics.
alex: timeline? canary starts in ~10m. ping here with results. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: scheduled run started at 5678901244
matt: thanks — if we still see p95 > 15ms on kernels we'll revert the kernel-selection patch and keep batching changes.
jia: noted. will collect traces and upload a short flamegraph link on completion.
alex: thanks all.
